meta.basis: Original questions authored from the Traffic Rules of the Republic of Uzbekistan (PDD, 29 chapters, as amended 12 April 2022) and current licensing regulations.
meta.disclaimer: Study aid only. Not an official government product and not affiliated with the DYHXX/SBDD. Always verify against the current official rules.

questions.question: Which set of documents must a driver of a passenger car be able to present to a traffic officer in Uzbekistan?
options: Driving licence, vehicle registration certificate and a valid compulsory third-party liability insurance policy
Vehicle registration certificate and a technical inspection receipt
questions.explanation: The rules require the licence for the relevant category, the vehicle registration certificate and a valid compulsory liability insurance policy. Holders of a biometric passport or ID card may have these verified digitally by the officer's tablet.

questions.question: What is the permitted blood alcohol level for a driver in Uzbekistan?
options: 0.5 promille, the same as most of Europe
None — driving under the influence of alcohol is prohibited outright
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan applies a zero-tolerance standard: a driver may not operate a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, narcotics or psychotropic substances, and may not hand the vehicle to someone who is.

questions.question: May a driver use a mobile phone while driving?
options: Only if the vehicle is equipped with hands-free equipment
Only when stopped at a red light
questions.explanation: Talking on a phone while driving is permitted only with hands-free equipment that leaves both hands free for control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Who is exempt from the requirement to wear a seat belt?
options: Nobody — everyone in the vehicle must be belted
Only the driver may be unbelted
Children under 12 seated in the rear, driving instructors while teaching, pregnant women and emergency service personnel on duty
questions.explanation: The seat belt requirement applies to every vehicle fitted with belts, with narrow exemptions including rear-seated children under 12, instructors during a lesson, pregnant women and emergency personnel performing their duties.

questions.question: You have stopped on the carriageway at night outside a populated area. What must you wear when you step out of the vehicle?
questions.explanation: A driver who leaves the vehicle on the carriageway in darkness or conditions of poor visibility must wear a reflective vest so as to be seen by other road users.

questions.question: In which of the following conditions is a driver prohibited from driving?
options: When feeling tired or unwell to a degree that affects road safety
When carrying more than three passengers
When the fuel tank is less than a quarter full
When driving a vehicle registered in another region
questions.explanation: A driver must not drive when fatigued or in a state of health that could compromise safety and the ability to control the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a category B (passenger car) licence in Uzbekistan?
questions.explanation: Category B is issued from the age of 18. Other categories have different minimum ages set by the licensing regulations.
questions.rule: Licensing regulations (Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 408)

questions.question: The theory exam consists of 20 questions. How many mistakes are you allowed and how long do you have?
questions.explanation: The theory exam is 20 single-answer questions in 25 minutes; you pass with at least 18 correct answers, so no more than 2 mistakes.

questions.question: A traffic light shows a flashing green signal. What does it mean?
options: Movement is permitted, but the signal is about to change
questions.explanation: A flashing green permits movement but warns that the permission is about to expire and a prohibiting signal will follow.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: A flashing yellow signal at an intersection means:
options: The traffic light is faulty and must be reported
Movement is permitted; the intersection is uncontrolled and you must apply the priority rules
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow allows movement but tells you the intersection is unregulated, so right-of-way is determined by signs and the general priority rules.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: The traffic light shows red together with yellow. What may you do?
options: Move off only if turning right
Nothing — movement is still prohibited; the combination warns that green is coming
questions.explanation: Red plus yellow still prohibits movement. It only informs drivers that a green signal is about to be switched on.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: The yellow signal comes on when you are so close to the stop line that stopping would require emergency braking. What should you do?
options: Brake as hard as necessary to stop before the line
Stop in the middle of the intersection
Reverse back behind the stop line
questions.explanation: Yellow prohibits movement, but a driver who cannot stop without emergency braking is permitted to continue. Emergency braking risks a rear-end collision.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: A traffic controller stands with both arms extended sideways. What does this mean for you if you are approaching him from the front?
options: Movement from the front and from behind him is prohibited; traffic from his sides may proceed
You must stop and switch off the engine
questions.explanation: With arms extended sideways (or lowered), traffic approaching the controller's chest and back is stopped; traffic approaching his left and right sides may move.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: The traffic controller raises his arm upwards. What does this signal mean?
options: Traffic is prohibited in all directions
Only vehicles turning right may proceed
questions.explanation: An arm raised vertically prohibits movement of all road users in every direction, apart from the narrow exceptions in the rules for drivers who cannot stop safely.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: The traffic controller's signals contradict the traffic light. Which do you follow?
options: The traffic light, because it is automatic
Neither — you must stop until they agree
questions.explanation: The signals and instructions of a traffic controller take precedence over traffic lights, road signs and markings.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: A green arrow pointing left is illuminated. Unless a sign forbids it, what else does this arrow permit?
questions.explanation: A signal permitting a left turn also permits a U-turn, unless a road sign in force at that location prohibits it.
questions.rule: Ch. 7 — Traffic light and controller signals

questions.question: You approach an unregulated intersection of two roads of equal importance. Who has right of way?
options: The vehicle approaching from the right
The vehicle approaching from the left
The vehicle going straight ahead, whichever side it comes from
questions.explanation: At an unregulated intersection of equal roads, a driver must give way to vehicles approaching from the right.

questions.question: At an unregulated intersection a tram and a car of equal road status arrive at the same time. Who goes first?
options: The car, if it is on the right
The car, because trams must always yield
questions.explanation: At unregulated intersections a tram has priority over wheeled vehicles travelling on a road of equal status, regardless of its direction of travel.

questions.question: You are turning left at an unregulated intersection on a road of equal status. Who must you give way to?
options: Nobody, if you signalled in time
Oncoming vehicles travelling straight ahead or turning right
Only vehicles that are already in the intersection
questions.explanation: When turning left or making a U-turn, you must give way to oncoming traffic proceeding straight ahead or turning right on a road of equal status.

questions.question: It is dark and you cannot tell whether the surface you are driving on is a main road; no priority signs are visible. What must you assume?
options: That you are on the main road
That you are on a secondary road and must give way
questions.explanation: If the type of road surface cannot be determined because of darkness, mud, snow or similar conditions and there are no priority signs, the driver must consider himself to be on a secondary road.

questions.question: A vehicle with a flashing blue beacon and a siren is approaching from behind. What must you do?
options: Brake sharply and stop where you are
Give way, clearing a path for it, without creating danger for other road users
Increase speed to stay ahead of it
Continue normally — the siren does not affect you
questions.explanation: When a vehicle displays a flashing blue beacon together with a special sound signal, drivers must give way and allow it a free passage, doing so safely rather than by braking abruptly.

questions.question: The main road changes direction at an unregulated intersection. How do drivers on the main road determine priority between themselves?
options: The driver going straight always has priority
By the rules for intersections of equal roads — give way to the right
The driver following the main road has priority over all others
Priority is determined by vehicle size
questions.explanation: Where the main road changes direction, drivers travelling on it apply the equal-road rules among themselves; drivers on the secondary road do the same among themselves.

questions.question: Traffic on the far side of an intersection is congested. May you enter the intersection on a green light?
options: No, if it would force you to stop inside and block crossing traffic
Yes, provided you sound your horn first
Only if you are turning right
questions.explanation: A driver must not enter an intersection, including on a permitting signal, if congestion would force him to stop within it and obstruct traffic crossing in another direction.

questions.question: What is the general speed limit for a passenger car in a populated area in Uzbekistan, where no sign says otherwise?
questions.explanation: The general limit in populated areas is 70 km/h, but note that Tashkent, Nukus, regional centres and urban settlements are limited to 60 km/h.

questions.question: You are driving in Tashkent on a street with no speed signs. What is your limit?
questions.explanation: In Tashkent, Nukus, regional centres and urban-type settlements the limit is 60 km/h — lower than the general 70 km/h for populated areas. This catches out many drivers.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed within 300 metres of a school or pre-school institution?
questions.explanation: Within 300 metres of schools and pre-school institutions the speed must not exceed 30 km/h.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed in a residential zone or a courtyard area (dvor)?
questions.explanation: In residential zones and adjacent courtyard territories the limit is 20 km/h, and pedestrians have priority over vehicles there.

questions.question: Outside a populated area, what is the maximum speed for a passenger car or a truck with a permitted maximum mass up to 3.5 tonnes?
questions.explanation: Outside populated areas cars and light trucks up to 3.5 tonnes may travel at up to 100 km/h, subject to any lower posted limit.

questions.question: Outside a populated area, what is the maximum speed for a motorcycle, a car towing a trailer, or a truck over 3.5 tonnes?
questions.explanation: These vehicles are limited to 80 km/h outside populated areas. Intercity buses and minibuses may do 90 km/h; a truck with a trailer is limited to 70 km/h.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed when towing another mechanical vehicle?
questions.explanation: Towing a mechanical vehicle is limited to 50 km/h on all roads, whatever the general limit.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for a vehicle carrying an organised group of children?
questions.explanation: Vehicles transporting organised groups of children are limited to 60 km/h on any road, as are trucks carrying people in the cargo area.

questions.question: Which of the following must a driver take into account when choosing speed, even below the posted limit?
options: Traffic intensity, the condition of the vehicle and load, road and weather conditions, and visibility
Only the presence of traffic police
questions.explanation: Speed must allow constant control of the vehicle, taking traffic intensity, vehicle and load condition, road and weather conditions and visibility into account. The posted limit is a ceiling, not a target.

questions.question: Before beginning to overtake, what must the driver make sure of?
options: Only that the road ahead is clear
That the lane he will use is free for a sufficient distance, no vehicle behind has begun to overtake him, the vehicle ahead is not signalling a left turn, and he can return to his lane safely
That he has signalled — nothing else is required
That the vehicle ahead has flashed its lights
questions.explanation: All four conditions must be satisfied before the manoeuvre starts, and the driver must signal his intention beforehand.

questions.question: The vehicle ahead of you has switched on its left turn signal. On which side may you overtake it?
options: Overtaking is forbidden in this situation
questions.explanation: A vehicle signalling a left turn must be overtaken on the right. In general the rules permit overtaking wheeled vehicles travelling in the same direction on either side, but this case is an exception.

questions.question: In which of the following places is overtaking prohibited?
options: On a straight road outside a populated area
On bridges, pedestrian crossings, and within 100 metres of a railway crossing
On any road with two lanes in each direction
questions.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited at regulated intersections, at unregulated intersections when on a secondary road, on bridges and overpasses, at pedestrian crossings, within 100 m before railway crossings, on hill crests and where visibility is limited.

questions.question: You are being overtaken. What are you forbidden from doing?
options: Increasing your speed or otherwise obstructing the overtaking vehicle
questions.explanation: A driver being overtaken must not increase speed or take any other action that would prevent the overtaking manoeuvre from being completed.

questions.question: Outside a populated area, a queue of vehicles has built up behind your slow-moving or oversized vehicle and overtaking is difficult. What should you do?
options: Move over to the right and, if necessary, stop to let the accumulated vehicles pass
Speed up until the queue disperses
Signal left to warn them not to overtake
questions.explanation: Drivers of slow or large vehicles must pull as far right as possible, and stop if necessary, to let the vehicles behind them past.

questions.question: You have completed an overtake. What must you do next?
options: Stay in the lane you used, if it is free
Return to your previously occupied lane
Signal to thank the other driver
questions.explanation: After overtaking the driver must return to the lane he previously occupied, having first made sure this is safe.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'stopping' and 'parking' in the traffic rules?
options: Stopping is a deliberate halt of up to 5 minutes, or longer if needed to board passengers or load goods; parking is a longer deliberate halt
Parking is only what happens in a marked car park
questions.explanation: Stopping is a halt of up to 5 minutes, or longer if it is needed for passengers to get in or out or for loading; anything beyond that is parking.
questions.rule: Ch. 1 & Ch. 13 — Definitions; stopping and parking

questions.question: Where is stopping prohibited?
options: On a pedestrian crossing and closer than 5 metres before it
Within 50 metres of any bus stop, on any road
questions.explanation: Stopping is prohibited on pedestrian crossings and within 5 metres before them, on level crossings, in tunnels, on bridges and overpasses where fewer than three lanes remain, and wherever the vehicle would obstruct traffic or hide a signal from other drivers.

questions.question: Your vehicle has broken down where stopping is prohibited. What must you do?
options: Leave it and go for help immediately
Switch on hazard warning lights, place a warning triangle and move the vehicle out of the prohibited place as soon as possible
Nothing — a breakdown excuses any position
questions.explanation: The driver must switch on the hazard warning lights, display the emergency stop sign (triangle) and take steps to remove the vehicle from the place where stopping is forbidden.

questions.question: Outside a populated area, on which side of the road may you park for a rest?
options: On the right side, on the shoulder — and if there is no shoulder, at the edge of the carriageway
In the middle of the carriageway with hazards on
questions.explanation: Outside populated areas a vehicle stopped for a long rest must be placed off the carriageway, on the shoulder or in a designated area, on the right-hand side.

questions.question: At what distance must the emergency stop sign (warning triangle) be placed outside a populated area?
options: At least 5 metres from the vehicle
At least 15 metres from the vehicle
At least 30 metres from the vehicle
questions.explanation: The triangle is placed at least 15 m from the vehicle in populated areas and at least 30 m outside them, and further if visibility requires it.

questions.question: You are driving at night on an unlit road and an oncoming vehicle is 150 metres away. What must you do?
options: Keep the high beam on until it passes
Switch from high beam to low beam
questions.explanation: High beam must be switched to low beam no later than 150 m before an oncoming vehicle, and earlier if the other driver signals that he is being dazzled.
questions.rule: Ch. 23 — Use of external lighting devices

questions.question: You have been dazzled by an oncoming vehicle's headlights. What must you do?
options: Speed up to pass the vehicle sooner
Switch on the hazard warning lights, slow down and stop without changing lanes
Steer to the right and continue at the same speed
Flash your own high beam in return
questions.explanation: A dazzled driver must switch on the hazard warning lights and, without changing lanes, reduce speed and stop.
questions.rule: Ch. 23 — Use of external lighting devices

questions.question: When must a motorcycle or scooter use low beam headlights?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and scooters must run low beam in daylight too, along with convoys, buses carrying organised groups of children, towing vehicles and vehicles carrying dangerous or oversized loads.
questions.rule: Ch. 23 — Use of external lighting devices

questions.question: Must headlights be used when driving through a tunnel?
options: Only if the tunnel is unlit
Yes, regardless of whether the tunnel is lit
Only if the tunnel is longer than 500 metres
questions.explanation: Headlights must be switched on in tunnels irrespective of the tunnel's own lighting.
questions.rule: Ch. 23 — Use of external lighting devices

questions.question: Your vehicle is parked at night on an unlit section of road. What lights must be on?
options: No lights at all, to save the battery
questions.explanation: A vehicle stopped or parked at night on an unlit road must show parking lights; in poor visibility low beam and fog lights may be used as well.
questions.rule: Ch. 23 — Use of external lighting devices

questions.question: In which situation must hazard warning lights be switched on?
options: When parking in a permitted place
When the vehicle is being towed, after a forced stop where stopping is prohibited, or when the driver has been dazzled
When driving through a populated area at night
questions.explanation: Hazard lights are required in an accident, on a forced stop where stopping is prohibited, when dazzled, when being towed and when boarding or alighting children from a marked vehicle.

questions.question: You are approaching a railway level crossing with no barrier and the traffic light is off. What must you do?
options: Cross without slowing, since no signal is showing
Stop, check that no train is approaching from either direction, then cross
Sound the horn and cross quickly
questions.explanation: A driver may only cross a level crossing after making sure that no train is approaching. Where visibility or signals are unclear, he must stop and verify before proceeding.

questions.question: Which of the following is prohibited at a railway level crossing?
options: Crossing in first or second gear
Overtaking, stopping on the crossing, and driving around a lowered barrier
questions.explanation: Drivers must not overtake at a crossing, stop on it, drive around lowered barriers or cross when a prohibiting signal is shown.

questions.question: Which of the following is prohibited on a motorway (avtomagistral)?
options: Reversing, U-turns, stopping outside designated areas, and vehicles unable to exceed 40 km/h
questions.explanation: Motorways prohibit pedestrians, animals, cycles, vehicles that cannot maintain more than 40 km/h, reversing, U-turns through the central reservation, and stopping outside designated parking areas.

questions.question: In a residential zone, who has priority?
options: Pedestrians — but they must not obstruct vehicles without need
questions.explanation: In residential zones pedestrians may use both the pavement and the carriageway and have priority, though they must not obstruct vehicles unnecessarily. The speed limit is 20 km/h.

questions.question: Leaving a residential zone or a courtyard onto a road, what must you do?
options: Give way to all other road users, including pedestrians
Give way only to vehicles coming from the right
questions.explanation: When leaving a residential zone or an adjacent territory, the driver must give way to all other road users.

questions.question: On a steep descent where two vehicles cannot pass each other, who must give way?
options: The vehicle closest to a passing place
questions.explanation: Where passing is difficult on a steep gradient, the driver travelling downhill must give way to the vehicle coming up.
questions.rule: Ch. 21 — Driving on steep descents and ascents

questions.question: A pedestrian has stepped onto an unregulated pedestrian crossing. What must you do?
options: Sound the horn to warn them
Give way and let them complete the crossing
Continue if you can pass at least a metre away
questions.explanation: At an unregulated pedestrian crossing the driver must give way to pedestrians who are crossing or have stepped onto the carriageway to cross.

questions.question: A vehicle in the adjacent lane has stopped at an unregulated pedestrian crossing. What must you do?
options: Stop as well and only proceed after making sure no pedestrian is crossing
questions.explanation: If a vehicle has stopped in front of a crossing, drivers in adjacent lanes may continue only after stopping and satisfying themselves that no one is crossing.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for a personal mobility device (e-scooter) ridden on a pavement?
questions.explanation: Users of personal mobility devices may travel at up to 10 km/h on pavements and pedestrian paths, and up to 20 km/h at the edge of the carriageway, and must give way to pedestrians.

questions.question: A bus marked as carrying an organised group of children has stopped with its hazard lights on. What must you do?
options: Slow down and, if necessary, stop to let the children pass
questions.explanation: Drivers approaching a stopped vehicle displaying the 'children' identification mark with hazards on must reduce speed and, if necessary, stop to let children get on or off safely.
questions.rule: Ch. 17 & Ch. 26 — Crossings; transport of people

questions.question: Where there is no pavement or verge, on which side of the carriageway should a pedestrian walk?
options: On the right, with the traffic
On the left edge, facing oncoming traffic
In the centre of the road
questions.explanation: Pedestrians walking on the carriageway must keep to the edge and move towards oncoming traffic so that they can see approaching vehicles.

questions.question: You are involved in a road accident with injuries. What is your first obligation?
options: Move your vehicle to clear the road
Stop immediately, switch on hazard lights, display the warning triangle, and give first aid to the injured and call an ambulance and the police
Exchange contact details and drive on
questions.explanation: The driver must stop, secure the scene with hazards and the triangle, take all measures to help the injured, call an ambulance and the police, and remain at the scene.
questions.rule: Ch. 3 — Driver obligations in a road accident

questions.question: An injured person is unconscious but breathing normally. What is the correct action?
options: Sit them upright and give them water
Place them in the recovery position on their side and keep monitoring their breathing
Leave them exactly as they are and do nothing
questions.explanation: An unconscious casualty who is breathing should be turned onto their side so the airway stays clear and vomit cannot be inhaled, with breathing checked continuously.

questions.question: A casualty has severe arterial bleeding from the arm. What should you do first?
options: Wash the wound thoroughly with water
Apply direct pressure to the wound and, if bleeding does not stop, a tourniquet above it, noting the time it was applied
Wait for the ambulance without touching the wound
questions.explanation: Arterial bleeding is the most urgent threat: apply firm direct pressure, then a tourniquet above the wound if needed, and record the time it went on.

questions.question: When should you move an injured person out of a crashed vehicle?
options: Always, immediately, to make them comfortable
Only when there is a direct threat to life such as fire, or when they need resuscitation that cannot be given in place
Only if they ask you to
questions.explanation: Moving a casualty risks aggravating spinal injuries, so it is justified only by an immediate danger such as fire or the need for resuscitation that cannot be performed where they lie.

questions.question: In an accident with no injuries and where the drivers agree on what happened, what are they permitted to do?
options: Record the scene, including vehicle positions, and clear the carriageway before completing the formalities as the rules require
Move the vehicles first and record nothing
Wait for the police in place no matter how long it takes
questions.explanation: Where there are no casualties, drivers must first record the position of the vehicles, traces and objects before clearing the carriageway, since obstructing traffic is itself an offence.
questions.rule: Ch. 3 — Driver obligations in a road accident

questions.question: Which defect makes further driving prohibited outright, rather than merely requiring you to drive to a repair place?
options: A faulty service brake system or steering
questions.explanation: Faulty service brakes, faulty steering, and inoperative wipers on the driver's side in rain or snow prohibit movement; other listed faults allow driving only to a place of repair or parking.

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted distance between vehicles on a flexible tow rope?
options: No limit, provided the rope is marked
questions.explanation: Flexible towing requires a distance of 4 to 6 metres, with the rope marked by warning flags or reflective panels; rigid towing must not exceed 4 metres.

questions.question: Which vehicle may not be towed on a flexible rope?
options: A vehicle with an automatic gearbox
A vehicle whose braking system is not working
A vehicle with a trailer coupling
questions.explanation: A vehicle with an inoperative braking system cannot be towed on a flexible rope; rigid towing or transport on a platform is required.

questions.question: By how much may a load project beyond the rear of the vehicle before it must be marked with a warning sign?
questions.explanation: A load projecting more than 1 metre beyond the rear (or more than 0.4 m beyond the outer edge of the front or rear lights on the sides) must be marked with the 'oversized load' sign, and with lights or reflectors at night.

questions.question: Is it permitted to tow a vehicle when visibility is less than 300 metres due to fog?
options: No — towing is prohibited in conditions of poor visibility
Yes, but only outside populated areas
questions.explanation: Towing is prohibited in icy conditions and when visibility is insufficient, since the combination is far harder to control and to see.

questions.question: A triangular sign with a red border and a white background is:
questions.explanation: Triangular signs with a red border warn of a hazard ahead. Round signs with a red border prohibit; blue round signs are mandatory.

questions.question: What does the yellow diamond sign with a white border mean?
options: You are on a priority (main) road
questions.explanation: The yellow diamond is the 'main road' sign: you have priority at the intersections it covers until the 'end of main road' sign appears.

questions.question: A downward-pointing triangle with a red border and white centre requires you to:
options: Give way to traffic on the crossing road
questions.explanation: This is the 'give way' sign: you must yield to traffic on the intersecting road, but you need not stop if the way is clear. The octagonal STOP sign requires an unconditional stop.

questions.question: What is required at an octagonal red STOP sign at an intersection?
options: Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop completely at the stop line or the edge of the intersecting carriageway, then give way
Stop only if another vehicle is visible
questions.explanation: The STOP sign requires a full stop at the stop line — or, if there is none, at the edge of the intersecting carriageway — before giving way.

questions.question: A solid single line marking the centre of the carriageway means:
options: It may be crossed when overtaking
It may be crossed only by public transport
It marks the edge of the carriageway
questions.explanation: A solid longitudinal line separating traffic streams must not be crossed. A broken line may be crossed; where a solid and a broken line run together, it may be crossed only from the broken side.

questions.question: Signs 3.20 ('overtaking prohibited') and 3.22 are in force. What are you forbidden to do?
options: Overtake other vehicles in the zone covered by the sign
questions.explanation: These signs prohibit overtaking in their zone of operation, which lasts until the corresponding 'end of prohibition' sign or the nearest intersection.

questions.question: You see a blue round sign with a white arrow pointing right. What does it mean?
options: You must turn right — it is a mandatory direction sign
There is a right bend ahead
questions.explanation: Blue circular signs are mandatory: they prescribe the direction of travel, unlike red-bordered circles, which prohibit.

questions.question: What does a white rectangular sign with a black settlement silhouette mark?
options: The start of a populated area, where the populated-area rules and speed limits apply
questions.explanation: The sign marks the beginning of a populated area on a white background, which brings the populated-area rules into force, including the speed limit and the ban on unnecessary horn use.
